title: Observability Escrow Gateway sidecar for VPC & on-prem ingest QoS
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers' telemetry bursts (traces/metrics/logs) can overwhelm perimeter collectors and downstream pipelines, causing cross-tenant QoS interference and SLO regressions. Existing perimeter proxies and collectors lack a single, deployable artifact that enforces tenant-level ingest credits, signs envelopes for replay-safety, and exposes clear telemetry for latency/error dashboards across Dedicated/VPC/on-prem environments.

Goal: Design and implement an "Observability Escrow Gateway" sidecar that sits in front of on-prem and VPC collectors. It should: 1) perform tenant-scoped ingress crediting (QoS buckets) and soft circuit-breaking, 2) attach replay-safe watermark headers and signed provenance envelopes to telemetry batches, 3) enrich traces with quick 'hook' attributes for runtime routing decisions (e.g., deployment-id, capacity-class, preferred-model-variant), 4) expose per-tenant latency/error/backpressure metrics to Console ingestion dashboards and 5) provide an operator playbook for capacity tuning and incident runbooks for collector backpressure.

Scope: PoC sidecar (go) + integration tests, two config modes (VPC and on-prem), control API for token rotation and QoS throttles, Prometheus metrics + OpenTelemetry exporting for downstream dashboards, and a lightweight admin UI for debugging incoming tenant credit state.

Non-goals: Full multi-cluster orchestration, persistent long-term buffering (beyond ephemeral ring buffers), or implementing new sampling algorithms server-side (we will surface signals for the sampling service to act on).

Success criteria: 1) no cross-tenant SLO regressions under 3x burst workload in preprod; 2) dashboards in Console showing per-deployment P50/P95 latency and error-rate correlated with credit exhaustion events; 3) replay-safe tags present on re-ingested traces and logs validated during a simulated restore test.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Kumar: Created ticket with initial requirements after incident postmortem (collector overload on res-47 customers). Linked incident notes and suggested PoC timeline.

2025-02-19 - Daniel Park: Spike completed — implemented a minimal Go sidecar that accepts batched OTLP HTTP, tracks per-tenant token buckets, and forwards signed batches to the collector. Observations: token bucket leak under heavy parallelism; need lock-free counters and sharded maps.

2025-02-24 - Marissa Cole (SRE): Load test with 50 tenants at 5x baseline shows graceful shedding for low-priority tenants but a pathological case when lots of small traces cause header amplification. Action: introduce batch coalescing and max-headers-per-batch guard.

2025-02-27 - Daniel Park: Implemented signed provenance envelopes (HMAC) and replay-watermark header (obs-watermark:v1). Added a config to toggle signing for on-prem air-gapped installs. Open PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1923.

2025-03-03 - Li Wei (Product): Reviewed metrics schema — requested per-tenant counters for: accepted_batches, dropped_batches_by_credit, forwarded_bytes, avg_forward_latency_ms, current_token_balance, last_rejection_reason. Also requested a dashboard wireframe to differentiate Dedicated vs Private cluster behavior.

2025-03-05 - Daniel Park: Refactor completed: replaced global mutex with sharded Atomics, added batch coalescer, and added admin endpoints (GET /v1/tenant/{id}/credits, POST /v1/rotate-ingest-token). Integration tests added to validate HMAC envelope acceptance by collector. Next: Console dashboard widgets and runbook docs.
2025-03-05 - Security Review Note: security_review_required set; sidecar signs provenance envelopes. Coordinate with Security for key rotation policy before rolling to Private customers.
next_steps: Finalize Prometheus metrics schema and register metric names in observability-standards

Create operator runbook: token tuning, emergency bypass, key rotation steps for HMAC envelopes
Schedule security review for key management and signing mode for air-gapped installs (contact: Security Eng)
